scope: AA amyloidosis as a complication of chronic inflammatory disease, including chronic arthritis.

keyRecommendations.text: AA deposits are mainly serum amyloid A, made by hepatocytes in response to IL-1, IL-6, and TNF.
Congo red avidity with metachromatic birefringence under polarised light remains the gold standard for identifying amyloid.
Proteinuria, including nephrotic syndrome, is the earliest and most frequent clue in chronic inflammatory disease and may be present in up to 95% of patients.

clinicalBottomLine: In a patient with chronic arthritis or another long inflammatory disease, heavy proteinuria should raise suspicion of AA amyloidosis. Confirm amyloid with Congo red and polarised light, type it as AA, and map organ deposits with SAP scintigraphy where that test is available.
notableCaveats: The review says RA, ankylosing spondylitis, chronic juvenile arthritis, inflammatory bowel disease, and hereditary periodic fevers together can account for up to 90% of recent cases in developed countries. That figure is not a rate for rheumatoid arthritis alone. The paper describes metachromatic birefringence, not a colour name.
